research_questions.main_original: How can a process-aware multimodal AI architecture be designed and evaluated for robust industrial anomaly detection using robotic welding data as a case study?
research_questions.SQ1: Which lightweight or pretrained Transformer-based representation components are suitable for visual, audio, and sensor time-series data in a multimodal industrial anomaly detection pipeline?
research_questions.SQ2: How do unimodal baselines, simple concatenation fusion, modular late fusion, and process-aware gated cross-modal fusion compare in terms of predictive performance?
research_questions.SQ3: Can a gated cross-modal fusion architecture improve robustness when one or more modalities are missing, degraded, or unreliable?
research_questions.SQ4: How can multimodal architecture performance be evaluated beyond accuracy, including robustness, interpretability, modularity, and practical usability?

search_themes.query: How are independently measured visual and sensor time-series modalities used in industrial monitoring and robotic failure detection?
When do pretrained visual or temporal representations outperform simple feature-based baselines under limited industrial labels?
Under what controlled evaluation conditions do concatenation, late fusion and gating improve on strong unimodal baselines, and when do they fail?
Does quality-conditioned fusion outperform exposure-matched static fusion under missing and degraded modalities while preserving clean performance?
How do proxy labels, group-disjoint splitting, stacking, calibration, class imbalance and uncertainty affect industrial multimodal evaluation?
What evidence distinguishes architecture or software reuse, native retraining, learned weight transfer and deployment readiness?

rules: State progression requires actual evidence; metadata verification does not verify a claim.
A passage supports only its bounded claim; abstracts cannot supply missing protocol details.
Track preprint/published versions as related records, not independent evidence.
All empirical numbers trace to result IDs and precise protocol definitions.
Keep proposed gap separate from established prior-art review.
Maintain one canonical manuscript; merge reviewed sections with a change record.
Record actual AI prompts prospectively; do not recreate unknown past prompts.
Human review confirms understanding and authorship; AI review is not independent human validation.
